answer: Lagoon Delay Accumulator. New identities must wait in an umber queue: each agent's first N actions are rate-limited to one per fixed interval, with interval length set by cohort size, so a burst of registrations spreads across time instead of arriving at once. A wharf-side admission gate releases identities only as earlier ones clear their delay. Sybil cost: an attacker pays wall-clock time per identity, not just fees, and parallel registration buys no speedup.
